messages.subject: Using tagAppendAttributes() more than once on the same tag
messages.subject_clean: Using tagAppendAttributes() more than once on the same tag
messages.body_plain:
I noticed that tag attributes are stored as a named list in the `attribs` value of a shiny.tag I wanted to add a class to a tag that already had a class, like so: shiny::tagAppendAttributes(shiny::div("hello", class = "foo"), class = "bar") This does work right and give me the desired output
hello
However, when I inspect the tag I see that the two classes are stored as two separate items List of 3 $ name : chr "div" $ attribs :List of 2 ..$ class: chr "foo" ..$ class: chr "bar" $ children:List of 1 ..$ : chr "hello" - attr(*, "class")= chr "shiny.tag" This feels wrong, though it's probably not technically wrong? I was hoping the class would be a string "foo bar" but instead it just added "bar" as another class. It does make it a bit more difficult to test for a specific class. I'm just wondering if there is a more correct way to do what I'm doing (adding multiple values of the same attribute but not all at once) and if this behaviour is correct or undesired. Thanks ShinyRs!

messages.subject_clean: Shiny Running a Single File Shiny App
messages.body_plain:
Jason,

The single file should be called "app.R", and in a directory of its own in the same location where you server your other Shiny applications (default is /srv/shiny-server). Then you can access it with the name of directory. For example:

http://localhost:3838/single-file-app

Hope this helps,
Fereshteh

messages.subject: Re: allow HTML in dataframe
messages.subject_clean: allow HTML in dataframe
messages.body_plain:
There is no argument called `alllowHTML` in renderDataTable(). There
is only `escape = FALSE`.

BTW, we will move to the new DT package for rendering DataTables in
the future: http://rstudio.github.io/DT/ The datatable() function also
has the `escape` argument.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: Saving a Reactive Variable as a Global Variable
messages.subject_clean: Saving a Reactive Variable as a Global Variable
messages.body_plain:
By the time server.R begins executing, ui.R is already done. So it doesn't make sense to try to use a reactive expression or value from ui.R; it has no way to respond to any changes that happen in the future.

Instead, check out renderUI <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/dynamic-ui.html>, which should do what you want.

Alternatively, if the value is something that won't change over time, you can define the variable in global.R and then access it from both ui.R and server.R.

messages.subject: Re: Why the same code is working only once
messages.subject_clean: Why the same code is working only once
messages.body_plain:
summary1 and summary2 are reactive expressions, and as such, neither can cause themselves to run; they need to actually be used by an output (or an observer), either directly or through another reactive expression.

In other words, reactive expressions are lazily loaded. For this reason, you rarely want to call print() from inside of them--that's an example of a side effect and reactive expressions should not be used for side effects, except maybe while you're debugging whether/why it is/isn't executing.

If you want summary2 to be called, either change reactive() to observe(), or create another observer and call summary() from it:
observe({
  summary2()
})

See these articles for more info:
http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/reactivity-overview.html
http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/execution-scheduling.html

Usually you'll just wrap it in a reactive expression, and use that from everywhere. There is such thing as reactive values but I'm not sure they're needed here.

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  helloKittyData <- reactive({
    validate(need(input$file1, "Please upload a file"))

    read.csv(input$file1$datapath)
  })

  output$contents <- renderTable({
    helloKittyData()
  })

  output$dynamicUI <- renderUI({
    checkboxGroupInput("columns", "Choose columns", names(helloKittyData()))
  })

Hi all,

Below you can find a screen capture from a shiny app that I'm building (I think you'll like what you'll see):
http://goo.gl/fHG4w5

For particular reasons, I've chosen an HTML + Javascript approach for the user interface. I would be curious if something like that can be done via shiny directly, but I guess this is just too customised.

Now about the subject of this email: when displaying the data (especially visible after setting the row.names argument), you can notice a 250ms delay that I determined are necessary for R to observe() the change in the Javascript object, then apply the read.csv() function and return the result back to Javascript.

250ms is not such a bad deal, but this is a very small dataset. I've tries with a larger one... and nothing. It seems that for larger(ish) datasets (for example 1000 rows and 300 columns) something happens with the communication between R and Javascript.

Could anyone point me to some kind of a possible solution?
I know there are shiny tables available, but I kind of like my data editor. Just curious how much data can I fit in this little tool.

Ideally, what I would like to achieve is a rich, highly interactive (and reactive) user interface that would be almost similar to any program installed on a local computer... and that would also imply editing a "normal" sized dataset.

Thanks,
Adrian

messages.subject: Re: uncaught exception: Duplicate binding for ID
messages.subject_clean: uncaught exception: Duplicate binding for ID
messages.body_plain:
I don't get the Javascript error when I run your app. Note that I'm using the latest development version of Shiny.

As for why the choice value isn't updating for you, it's because this is what you're using to update the value:

  observe({
    selected.choice <<- input$select
  })

And then you access `selected.choice` from various renderUI functions, like this:

  output$text.main.outA1 = renderPrint({
    cat("This is A, with selection ",input$A, " and selected choice: ",selected.choice)
  })

When input$select changes, it won't invalidate that renderPrint() -- it will only invalidate the observer.

If you want changes in input$select to cause the renderPrint() to re-execute, you need to do one of the following:

* Access input$select directly in renderPrint().

* Use a reactive expression, like this:
    selected_choice <- reactive( input$select )
  and then access selected_choice() from your renderPrint().

* Use a reactiveValues object and assign a value into it, in the observe(). Then access it in the renderPrint().

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Cannot get eventReactive to work
messages.subject_clean: Cannot get eventReactive to work
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tim, can you try something like this?

shinyServer(
    function(input, output){
        lookups <- eventReactive(input$predict, {
            # do lookups and return a result
        })

        output$next_word <- renderText({
            lookups()
        })
     }
)

When you call output$next_word <- renderText(...), this isn't giving a command to "render next_word right now" or anything; what you're saying instead, is "this is how one would go about rendering next_word". So you only ever want to make that assignment once, and if the body of the renderText(...) uses reactive expressions or reactive values, then it'll automatically know when it should execute and re-execute.

messages.subject: Generate observeEvent procedurally
messages.subject_clean: Generate observeEvent procedurally
messages.body_plain:
Good evening,

(me again, I'm afraid...)

I'm now building an interface with several sliders, let's call them A, B and C for now. In the real app there will be an arbitrary number of them, and their names will be generated by reading a file containing their names -- I've been that far. These sliders represent quantities whose sum must always be equal to 100%, so increasing the amount of A should decrease the value of B and C, and this should reflect on the sliders.

The solution I found so far is to use observeEvent on each slider, and call updateSliderInput from there, and this piece of code works fine:

observeEvent(input$sla,{ # slider A is called input$sla
aa<-input$sla

ee<-c(input$slb,input$slc)
names(ee)<-c("b","c")
ee_n<-ee/sum(ee)*(100-aa)
 updateSliderInput(session,"slb",
                       value=as.numeric(ee_n["b"]))
 updateSliderInput(session,"slc",
                       value=as.numeric(ee_n["c"]))

},ignoreNULL=T)

There may be better way, but this works. When A is moved, B and C change so that the total is kept to 100, and the relative proportion of B to C is preserved.

Now, I need to generate one such observer for each slider. Relatively easy if there is only a handful of them and if they are known already, but how can I do that for an arbitrary number of sliders ? I tried something like

slidernames<-c("a","b","c")
for(m in slidernames){
observeEvent(input[[paste("sl",m,sep="")]],{
   cat("Slider",m,"\n")
# Placeholder for more clever stuff, but demonstrates that m is used here too !
    })
}

but this does not seem to work (with this example, moving any slider gives "Slider c", which is not really good...).

So my immediate question is "how to generate several event observers?". But I'm willing to take any hint on the larger problem :-)

With thanks,

Jeff

messages.body_plain:
Shiny has a new function called eventReactive that should help with this. Basically the eventReactive itself only invalidates itself when input$Run is clicked. And if you try to access the reactive before it's been run for the first time, it'll raise a silent validation error <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/validation.html>.

### This needs to update first

  tweets <- eventReactive(input$Run, {
    searchString=input$searchString
    numberOfTweets=input$numTweets
    searchTwitter(searchString,numberOfTweets)

  })

### Now plot with the new data
  output$tweetPerson <- renderPlot({

    plot(tweets()) # or whatever
  })

  output$tweetTime <- renderPlot({
    plot(tweets()) # or whatever
  })

messages.body_plain:
I suspect your for-loop doesn't work because the "m" variable is shared across invocations (a weird quirk of R). Can you try it with lapply instead of for?

For your bonus question--I think it'd be nice to create the observers at the same time as the sliders.

slidernames <- reactive({ ... })
output$sliders <- renderUI({
  lapply(slidernames(), function(slidername) {
    observeEvent(input[slidername], {...})
    sliderInput(slidername, slidername, ...)
  })
})

By the way, if it's possible for this renderUI to happen more than once, and if it's possible for the same slidernames to repeat over time, you'll want to make sure any previously defined observeEvents are suspended. observeEvent() returns an object you can call $suspend() on.

messages.subject: making observers using a loop (for or lapply)
messages.subject_clean: making observers using a loop (for or lapply)
messages.body_plain:
Just a little solution in case anyone finds it useful.
It took me a while to figure this out.

If you want to put a set of observe() objects in your shiny server session
using a for() or lapply(),
the call to observe() needs to assign the observer to a variable name.
Otherwise, only the last value takes hold.

Thus this example works fine,
but if you leave out the assign statement,
only observer #7 is registered in the server:

  obs = function(number)
    assign("obs" %&% number,
           observe({
             newValue <- input[["stepStatus" %&% number]]
             catn("Toggling stepStatus" %&% number %&% " = " %&% newValue)
             isolate({ # necessary, or else crash!
               rValues$stepsTable[number, "Done?"] = newValue
               catn("New value in stepsTable: ",
                    rValues$stepsTable[number, "Done?"] )
             })
           }
           )
    )
  lapply(1:7, obs)

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Problem with updateSelectInput using tabpanel
messages.body_plain:
The problem is using observe strategy to update when you are using renderUI and uiOutput. I fix that using reactive strategy like that

The reactive approach with selectInput:
outVar <- reactive({
 vars <- all.vars(parse(text=as.character(input$inBody)), functions = FALSE, unique = TRUE)
 vars <- as.list(vars) return(vars) })

output$inVar2 <- renderUI({
 selectInput(inputId = "inVar2", label = h4("2. Select a variable:"), choices = outVar())
})

And use uiOutput(inVar2) inside mi principal renderUI

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm trying to switch from a tab to another on by clicking a button. I almost succeeded, i just need to highlight the "good" tab in the sidebar. Any hint ?

library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

server = function(input, output) {
  output$button <- renderUI({
    tags$button("Click to switch tab", "class"="btn btn-default action-button",
                "data-toggle"="tab", "href"="#shiny-tab-tab2")
  })
}

ui = dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(),
  dashboardSidebar(
    sidebarMenu(
      menuItem("Tab1", tabName = "tab1"),
      menuItem("Tab2", tabName = "tab2"))
  ),
  dashboardBody(
    tabItems(
      tabItem("tab1",uiOutput("button")),
      tabItem("tab2", "tab2", "Done !")
    )
  )
)
runApp(list(ui=ui,server=server))

Thanks for helping,
Matthieu

messages.subject: Re: making observers using a loop (for or lapply)
messages.subject_clean: making observers using a loop (for or lapply)
messages.body_plain:
I was asked for more details, so here:

I have a set of 7 radio button sets as part of seven sections.

In ui.R, I place calls to sectionHeader(), defined as:
sectionHeader = function(number) {
  list(hr(),
       h2(paste0('(', number, ') ',
                 stepsTableInitial[number, "Stepping stone"])),
       h3("Question " %&% number, ": ",
          stepsTableInitial[number, "Question"]),
   span(
     radioButtons("stepStatus" %&% number,
                 label="Is this step done?", choices=c("Not yet", "Done"))
   )
}

The radioButton ID’s are stepStatus1 … stepStatus7.
The observers created in server.R allow the interface to respond to radioButton clicks:
update values in a tableOutput, enable or disable a button, ...

But, the point is that without the “assign” wrapper,
    assign("obs" %&% number,...)
only the last radioButton set is observed.

I hope this helps!

On Saturday, April 11, 2015 at 3:05:55 PM UTC-4, Roger Day wrote:
> Just a little solution in case anyone finds it useful.
> It took me a while to figure this out.
>
> If you want to put a set of observe() objects in your shiny server session
> using a for() or lapply(),
> the call to observe() needs to assign the observer to a variable name.
> Otherwise, only the last value takes hold.
>
> Thus this example works fine,
> but if you leave out the assign statement,
> only observer #7 is registered in the server:
>
>   obs = function(number)
>     assign("obs" %&% number,
>            observe({
>              newValue <- input[["stepStatus" %&% number]]
>              catn("Toggling stepStatus" %&% number %&% " = " %&% newValue)
>              isolate({ # necessary, or else crash!
>                rValues$stepsTable[number, "Done?"] = newValue
>                catn("New value in stepsTable: ",
>                     rValues$stepsTable[number, "Done?"] )
>              })
>            }
>            )
>     )
>   lapply(1:7, obs)

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

On your guys Rstudio support site you have a guide called "Code Folding and Sections":
https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/200484568-Code-Folding-and-Sections

In it it says:
> Edit -> Folding:
> Collapse — Alt+L
> Expand — Shift+Alt+L
> Collapse All — Alt+A
> Expand All — Shift+Alt+A
However, when I open up the R-studio it says "Collapse ALL Alt+O", and "Expand All Alt+Shift+O". It is also correct in the keyboard shortcut resources:
https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/200711853-Keyboard-Shortcuts

I post there here as friendly suggestion that "Code Folding and Sections" guide be updated. :)

Thanks,
Reino

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Yihui,

I didn't know about debug(httpuv::service) as a tool. Pretty cool. I will have to use it more often on some of my sourced functions. The little red dot doesn't always work for me.

So I sorted out the "NAs introduced by coercion" warning last night be rewritting all.is.numeric with a suppresswarning. It is weird that the two nearly identical computers handled that differently.

I just tested the fix on the crashing computer, and it seems to work. Weird how such a tiny warning would have such a whole effect.

cause instead of sweeping the issue under the carpet by
suppressWarnings().

Yihui

messages.subject: Passing reactive values to functions and accessing reactive attributes
messages.subject_clean: Passing reactive values to functions and accessing reactive attributes
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I want to take a reactive source through more than one reactive conductor before sending it to a reactive endpoint.

Generalized example:

x <- reactive({ function(input$var) })

y<-reactive({ function(x) })

output$display<-renderText({ y()$attr })

Below is a specific Example.

Thanks in advance,

Sam

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

# Install packages if needed
packageNeeds <- c('shiny', 'httr', 'dataRetrieval')
packageNeeds <- packageNeeds[!packageNeeds %in% rownames(installed.packages())]
if(length(packageNeeds)>0){
  install.packages(packageNeeds, repos='http://cran.cnr.Berkeley.edu')
}

library(shiny)
library(httr)
library(dataRetrieval)

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    fluidRow(
            wellPanel(
              selectInput("site", label = p("Pick a site"), choices = list('01594440', 'sysys')),
              selectInput("start", label = p("pick a date"), choices = list('1985-01-01', "xyz")))),
    fluidRow(wellPanel(verbatimTextOutput("URL"))),
    fluidRow(wellPanel(verbatimTextOutput("REC")))),
  server = function(input, output, session){
    url<-reactive({
      # Here the user inputs are used to constuct a url -
      # but really this could be any function that I'd like to take the output of
      # and pass it on to other functions and/or subeset
      # before sending to a reactive output
      constructWQPURL(paste("USGS",input$site,sep="-"),
                            c('01075','00029','00453'),
                            input$start, endDate = "")
      })
    # This is the function I've passed the reactive value to
    # it returns an object with a headers attributes that has the
    # 'total-result-count' attribute I want
    header_call = reactive({HEAD(url)})

    output$URL<-renderText({
      # The url displays fine
       url()
    })
    output$REC<-renderText({
      # The record count from the header pull does not display
      # the value is the number of records stored as a string
      header_call()$headers$'total-result-count'
    })
  }
)

>  “I suggested you debug httpuv::service, and see what exactly the value of timeoutMs is (which you did not tell us), and why R failed to coerce it to a numeric value. “

I had to undo my “fix” so that I could show you what happens Yihui. This is the verbatim code what is the culprit. It is pretty much verbatim from the function all.is.numeric {Hmisc}. I use it inside of another function.

all.is.numeric2 <- function (x, what = c("test", "vector"), extras = c(".", "NA")) {
  what <- match.arg(what)
  old <- options(warn = -1)
  on.exit(options(old))
  x <- sub("[[:space:]]+$", "", x)
  x <- sub("^[[:space:]]+", "", x)
  xs <- x[x %nin% c("", extras)]
  # suppressWarnings(isnum <- !any(is.na(as.numeric(xs))))
  isnum <- !any(is.na(as.numeric(xs)))  if (what == "test")
    isnum
  else if (isnum)
    as.numeric(x)
  else x
}

It only crashes the app when suppressWarnings() is not being used. Crashes are intermitting, and varied in what exactly crashes. I have gotten:

  1) Error in eval(substitute(expr), envir, enclos) :  cncompatible lengths for set aesthetics: fontface, label
  2) I have had it just crash.
  3) Sometimes it kicks out 50 NA coercion warnings and then turns off.
  4) Sometimes the exact same code produces no warnings at all, and runs fine.

When I am able to catch the warning, it shows that it was provoked by strings of characters going into the as.numeric() function as intended.

When I run it with debug(httpuv::service) in the pre-server function script, the bug tracker drops into the code below and keeps loading 100, and never stops. It seems impossible to advances the webapp when I press continue a million times.

“service” function.

The function is defined:

Okay, the use of suppressWarning() in that case is completely
legitimate in my eyes. FWIW, Frank (author of Hmisc) has considered
suppressing the warning by options(warn = -1), but that is actually
not the appropriate way to suppress warnings for a particular
expression in R: suppressWarnings() should be the correct way. There
is a subtle difference between the two ways
(https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues/610). I suggest you write to
Frank, and recommend him to use suppressWarnings() instead of
options(warn = -1).

I do not see significant differences between the two R sessions:
https://www.diffchecker.com/vmzd3js8 I do not understand why the
warning messages can be different on the two computers.

Regards,
Yihui

Am comfortable applying the suppressWarning() myself. If I really wanted to fix the problem, I would make a new function in Rcpp. Modeling it off of as.numeric() which is just an method for .Primitive("as.double").

>From names.c:
/* Type coercion */
{"as.double", do_ascharacter, 2, 1, -1, {PP_FUNCALL, PREC_FN, 0}},

>From coerce.c:
/* the "ascharacter" name is a historical anomaly: as.character used to be the
 * only primitive;  now, all these ops are : */
SEXP attribute_hidden do_ascharacter(SEXP call, SEXP op, SEXP args, SEXP rho)
{
...
    case 2:
    name = "as.double"; type = REALSXP; break;
...
}
/*Which gets plopped into isna later..*/
SEXP attribute_hidden do_isna(SEXP call, SEXP op, SEXP args, SEXP rho)
{...
    case REALSXP:
    for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
        LOGICAL(ans)[i] = ISNAN(REAL(x)[i]);
...}

So it is really just a quick for loop which returns a logical array.

If I want this process to be optimized, I would just make a simple vector scan in c++.

messages.subject: Re: Browse for filesystem
messages.subject_clean: Browse for filesystem
messages.body_plain:
Then for that, maybe you could do something like this using file.choose:

> library(shiny)
>
> ui <- fluidPage(
>   actionButton('browse', 'Browse'),
>   textOutput("chosenPath")
> )
>
> server <- function(input, output, session) {
>   filePath <- eventReactive(input$browse, {
>     file.choose()
>   })
>
>   output$chosenPath <- renderText({
>     filePath()
>   })
> }
>
> shinyApp(ui, server)

This only works if the browser and the Shiny process are running on the same machine, since file.choose() will pop up the file dialog on the server, not on the client.

If you want to upload a file from the client, you can use fileInput().

If you want to choose a file that's on the server AND the browser and server aren't on the same machine, then neither of the previous approaches will work. If the data directory isn't too large, maybe you could list all of the possible files as choices in a selectInput. (Just make sure to verify that the user input that comes back is indeed in your data directory--it's always possible for a malicious visitor to ignore the valid choices your app provides and send arbitrary values to your app.)

messages.subject: Problem when reloading an animated GIF in Chrome
messages.subject_clean: Problem when reloading an animated GIF in Chrome
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm facing a strange problem when reloading an animated GIF that only shows when using Google Chrome (Firefox and Internet Explorer don't show the problem). I've tested it in Chrome 42.0.2311.90, Firefox 37.0.1 and Internet Explorer 9.0.8112.16421.

I want to include an animated GIF that shows a 1-second animation (it does not loop forever, i.e. it shows the animation and ends) in my Shiny application. More specifically, I want to show the animation every time an action button is pressed.

I have included in my ui.R file an imageOutput ("animated_image", the placeholder for the animated gif) and the corresponding actionButton ("show").

Then I have included the following code in my server.R file:

output$animated_image <- renderImage({
    input$show
    list(src="www/anim_1.gif")
}, deleteFile = FALSE)

when I load the application on Chrome, the animation only runs once (the first time the code is run). After that, whenever I press the button the image stays the same, just showing the last frame of the animated GIF. However, if I load it on Firefox or IE the application behaves as desired, i.e. the animation runs each time I press the button.

Fearing some problem related with image caching, I created a second version of the animated GIF with a slight modification in some pixels (so that it doesn't identify it as the same file) and stored it as "anim_2.gif". After that, I modified the code so that it loads alternatively the 1st or the 2nd version, hoping that the browser sees it as a different image than the previous one. This is the code (variable COUNT is previously initialized with 0):

output$animate_image <- renderImage({
    COUNT <- COUNT + input$show
    if (COUNT %% 2 == 0){filename="www/anim_1.gif"}
        else {filename="www/anim_2.gif"}
    list(src=filename)
}, deleteFile = FALSE)

In this case, the animation runs just twice (the first time the code is run, and after pressing the button for the first time). After that, it seems like Chrome detects that I'm trying to load an image that has already been loaded before (even if it is not the immediate previous one) and "refuses" to load the animation again. Firefox and IE still work fine.

I've also tried some solutions I found for related problems in other contexts, e.g. adding a random number as an additional parameter in the URL, like this:

list(src=paste0("www/anim_1.gif?x=",abs(rnorm(1))))

but that doesn't work in this case, as Shiny can't find the image with that tweaked URL.

Any ideas on how can I solve this problem that only shows in Chrome?

Thanks,
Mikel

messages.body_plain:
Martin and Michael are right that you should use data_user() when retrieving the value. I'd like to further point out that attempting to mutate the reactive expression doesn't make a lot of sense, as in the left-hand side of this:

data_user()$date <- as.Date(data_user()$date)

Instead you should either make a temporary variable in the renderPlot call, or (much) better yet, do the as.Date conversion right within the data_user reactive expression.

messages.subject: Re: Problem when reloading an animated GIF in Chrome
messages.subject_clean: Problem when reloading an animated GIF in Chrome
messages.body_plain:
The reason that changing the name with a '?' won't make a difference is because Shiny actually converts the image to a base64 encoded string, and sends that over to the browser. So the browser doesn't see a '?' at all, just the image data.

It sounds like this may be related to the way that Chrome caches images:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/10730212/proper-way-to-reset-a-gif-animation-with-displaynone-on-chrome

There's also a bit of JS code at the link which says it will restart a gif, though it may be a bit of work to get that to work with Shiny. You might be able to bypass Shiny entirely and just show/hide the content when a button is pressed, by creating a button with an onclick property:
  <button onclick="myFunction()">Click me</button>

To generate that same code in Shiny, you'd do something like:
  tags$button(onclick = "myFunction()", "Click me")

And then you'd have to embed Javascript code in your app to implement myFunction().

-Winston

Thank you very much, Winston! I have solved the problem following your suggestions.

Now my ui.R code looks like this:

sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(.....
        tags$button("show", onclick = "reset_anim()"),
        .....
    ),
    mainPanel(.....
        div(imageOutput("animated_image"), .....),
        .....,
        tags$head(tags$script(src="script.js"))
    )
)

And script.js (stored in the www folder) contains the following JavaScript code:

function reset_anim() {
    var div_elem = document.getElementById("animated_image");
    var img_elem = div_elem.getElementsByTagName("img")[0];
    var src_value = img_elem.getAttribute("src");
    img_elem.setAttribute("src", "");
    img_elem.setAttribute("src", src_value);
}

Now everything works like a charm in all browsers, thanks!

Cheers,
Mikel

messages.body_plain:
Hey Joe,

I was wondering if you could provide a little more detail on the new version of leaflet. When is it planned to support Shiny as fully as the old package? Also, we are investigating the possibility of heavily contributing to this package, so adding more comments might be helpful. There are quite a few features we need to add to make it viable, WMS, esri WMS, feature requests, methods to enable changes without redraws, non-standard WMS projections, drawing tools, etc - I'm not sure which if any of these you plan to implement.

Thanks,

Chris

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Has anyone tested performance of Shiny with Revolution Open R?

http://www.revolutionanalytics.com/revolution-r-open

I suppose performance benefits should large come from use cases that rely on matrix and vector operations.  I know I could install this on my own box running shiny server/R and test things out, but figured I'd ask about others' experiences before I take any time.

Does anyone familiar with the inner workings of Shiny have any insight to the benefits/drawbacks of using Revolution Open R?

Erik

messages.subject_clean: leaflet-shiny & heatmap
messages.body_plain:
We'll begin work on the full Shiny support on Monday (which is essentially "methods to enable changes without redraws" I believe). We're also currently working on legend support. Also on the list for the near term is support for some plugins, layer chooser control, raster/image layers, and possibly support for projections besides web mercator.

As for the other features, I'd love to video chat with you and get a better sense of these features as well as what you're trying to accomplish with Leaflet. We can also discuss ways your team can contribute. If you'd be open to chatting, please email me off-list and we can find a time next week to do that.

Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
You really should use the CRAN repository instead of the official
Ubuntu repo. The version of R in the latter is often years behind the
latest version of R. You can easily add the CRAN repo on
Ubuntu/Debian:

sudo apt-add-repository -y "deb http://cran.rstudio.com/bin/linux/ubuntu `lsb_release -cs`/"
sudo apt-key adv --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com <http://keyserver.ubuntu.com> --recv-keys E084DAB9
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get upgrade

More info: http://cran.rstudio.com/bin/linux/ubuntu/

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
Cheers for replying Joe - where would I put the statement, eg. in your output example if I'm trying something like:

library(shiny)

source("linechart.R")

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    # addResourcePath('www', 'www'),
    tags$h2("JavaScript output binding example"),
    fluidRow(
      column(width=6,
             p("This Shiny app is an adaptation of the",
               a(href="http://nvd3.org/examples/line.html", "Simple Line Chart"),
               "example for the",
               a(href="http://nvd3.org/", "NVD3.js"),
               "JavaScript charting library."
             ),
             p("Source code:",
               a(href="https://github.com/jcheng5/shiny-js-examples/tree/master/output", "@jcheng5/shiny-js-examples/output"))
      )
    ),
    fluidRow(
      column(width=9,
             lineChartOutput("mychart")
      ),
      column(width=3,
             sliderInput("sinePhase", "Sine phase", -180, 180, 0, step=10,
                         animate=animationOptions(interval=100, loop=TRUE)),
             sliderInput("sineAmplitude", "Sine amplitude", -2, 2, 1, step=0.1,
                         animate=animationOptions(interval=100, loop=TRUE))
      )
    )
  ),
  server = function(input, output, session) {

    output$mychart <- renderLineChart({
      # Return a data frame. Each column will be a series in the line chart.
      data.frame(
        Sine = sin(1:100/10 + input$sinePhase * pi/180) * input$sineAmplitude,
        Cosine = 0.5 * cos(1:100/10),
        "Sine 2" = sin(1:100/10) * 0.25 + 0.5
      )
    })
  }
)

messages.subject: Re: shinyApp www folder js/html/css
messages.subject_clean: shinyApp www folder js/html/css
messages.body_plain:
(Sorry for the terseness, I'm attending a class)

You need to make sure addResourcePath has been called before a browser requests those JS/CSS/image resources. There's no reason to assume this would be before the server function runs, and in fact I'd assume on a fresh R process that would probably not work. I'd assume the order is something like 1) web page requested, 2) JS/CSS/image requested, 3) connection to server established. You're probably seeing it work because addResourcePath only needs to be called once per R process--its effects last until that process ends.

The example is minimalized, of course. The gist of it is that with two sliders, input.x and input.y, I adjust the number of plots in a grid. In the actual application, I can then assign stuff to be plotted; I can then select a "compound" on the sidebar for which all that stuff would be plotted.

The plots are displayed with uiOutput, which is a dynamically generated output with named plots. This was adapted from something I found here: https://gist.github.com/wch/5436415

By and large this works great, but what I have trouble with is that I want to catch clicks on the plots.

The output element with the plots is built as follows:
>   # Insert the right number of plot output objects into the web page
>   output$plots <- renderUI({
>     r.y <- lapply(1:input$panel.y, function(panels.y)
>     {
>       r.x <- lapply(1:input$panel.x, function(panels.x)
>         {
>         plotname <- paste("plot",panels.x,panels.y, sep="-")
>         clickname <- paste(plotname, "click", sep="-")
>         column(width= 12/input$panel.x, plotOutput(plotname, clickId=clickname))
>       })
>       do.call(fixedRow, r.x)
>     })
>     #do.call(tagList, r.x)
>   })

The plot itself is plotted as follows:
>   # The actual plotting function
>   observe({
>     # replot on change of panel settings
>     input$panel.x
>     input$panel.y
>
>     # replot on selecting a new compound
>     input$cpd
>     row <- as.integer(input$cpd)
>     # note: in reality, I also replot in other cases.
>
>     for(panels.y in 1:input$panel.y) {
>       for(panels.x in 1:input$panel.x) {
>
>         local({
>
>           inputname <- paste("file",panels.x,panels.y, sep="-")
>           plotname <- paste("plot",panels.x,panels.y, sep="-")
>
>           output[[plotname]] <- renderPlot({
>             plot.new <http://plot.new>()
>             title(main=paste(inputname, row))
>
>           })
>
>         }) #local
>       } # for panels.x
>     } # for panels.y
>
>   }) # observe

This works great, but the "clickname" part is new. What I have to do now, is to dynamically build observers for every clickId when the panel.x or panel.y are changed. An observe() within an observe() doesn't really work and I am basically just trying random combinations of observe() isolate() reactive() and such, since I have not a deep enough understanding of the interdependencies that I would be able to approach this with an actual concept :). The one in the code right now is of course not working. Does anyone of you have experience with something like this?

What I believe would work, is to pre-generate observers for the maximum number of plots possible, which will just not be triggered as long as there are no plots there. (Hm, can you actually generate a dependency on an input which doesn't exist yet?) However this would be boring and not elegant, I'm really looking for the clean way to dynamically generate the observer when it is needed... Or some other "nice" solution...

Thanks for any help!

messages.subject: Re: Dynamically generating observers within observe()...?
messages.subject_clean: Dynamically generating observers within observe()...?
messages.body_plain:
You CAN nest observers, in fact. Just be aware that each time the outer observer runs, it's creating a new set of observers (while the previously created observers continue to exist and run). So I'd keep track of the sets of observers you've already created, and when input$panel.y/input$panel.x change, just create the ones that don't yet exist.

Also just because you asked, yes, you can generate a dependency on an input which doesn't exist yet. If you call input$foo it'll just be NULL, and when it later gets set you'll be notified.

And finally just because I have a feeling this might be relevant to you in the future, when you call observe() you actually get an object back that can be used to suspend, resume, or destroy the observer. See ?observe for details.

Hi!

I have a dynamic app (similar to this one <http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/superzip-example.html> ) in which I have some cities mapped out, and when the user clicks on a specific city, the app gives them information about it. All the info comes out of a data frame and everything works fine in the app. The thing is, I want the users to be able to download a PDF file specific to the city they clicked on. I have a .Rmd file prepared (as all the PDF's would have the same type of information, except it should be specific to the city, aka density, financial independece, etc.) but I can't find a way to link it to the shiny app, as in make the PDF display the name of the city and all of its specific information. I am able to download a "standard" PDF from the app--non reactive--, but I don't know if it is possible to make it reactive to the shiny app without having to make a specific file for each city?

The code I am using to download the pdf is this (and works fine):

output$downloadpdf <- downloadHandler(

    filename= "Report.pdf",

    content = function(file) {
      out = rmarkdown::render("Report.Rmd")
      file.rename(out, file)
    },

    contentType = 'application/pdf'
  )

And if I type this in my .Rmd to display the name of the chosen city (which is the same code I have in my server.R to display the name of the city):

```{r}
 output$zona.metropolitana.name <http://zona.metropolitana.name>

 ````
when I try downloading the PDF, it only renders this in a blank page:
"Reading objects from shinyoutput object not allowed rmarkdown"

So, again, is there a way to  make my .Rmd (PDF) file reactive to my shiny app??

Thank you for your help!
Margarita

messages.subject: popovers or popover buttons for radioButton choices
messages.subject_clean: popovers or popover buttons for radioButton choices
messages.body_plain:
Hello Shiny wizards!

I'm comfortable with R, fairly friendly with Shiny, but weak in the JavaScript skillset.

My question: For elements that are built for you by Shiny, such as the element built by the radioButtons() function, is there a way to add popovers to or beside features of the element?

Let's use, for example, the really basic radioButtons demo provided in the Shiny Widget Gallery <http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/widget-gallery.html>.

server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # You can access the values of the widget (as a vector)
  # with input$radio, e.g.
  output$value <- renderPrint({ input$radio })

})
ui.R
shinyUI(fluidPage(

  # Copy the line below to make a set of radio buttons
  radioButtons("radio", label = h3("Radio buttons"),
    choices = list("Choice 1" = 1, "Choice 2" = 2, "Choice 3" = 3),
    selected = 1),

  hr(),
  fluidRow(column(3, verbatimTextOutput("value")))

))
How would I go about modifying this code so that a user could click on each radio button choice (e.g., "Choice 1") and get a text description of that choice ("This is the first choice. Click it if you want to.")

This is similar to the question posed here <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/hover/shiny-discuss/6Jnmhpz5lJQ/_FyGSam50RwJ> about sliderInputs, which references the nifty shinyBS package <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/shinyBS/shinyBS.pdf>. However, the shinyBS solutions (bsPopover, popify, and addPopover) add popovers to an entire element. This is fine if you are generating a collection of separate elements (e.g., a set of sliders, each defined separately) but - as best I can tell - can't be used to specify popovers for features of an element.

Thank you in advance for any time and help you have to share!!

PS - This is my first post to the group - feel free to tell me if I'm failing to follow any posting etiquette or best practice!

messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to make a Rmarkdown file reactive to a shiny app??
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to make a Rmarkdown file reactive to a shiny app??
messages.body_plain:
Maybe try this:

    content = function(file) {
      inputEnv <- new.env()
      inputEnv$city <- input$city  # or whatever
      inputEnv$cityData <- cityData()
      out = rmarkdown::render("Report.Rmd", envir = inputEnv)
      file.rename(out, file)
    },

Then in your Rmd document you should be able to refer to city/cityData and get the values that you assigned to inputEnv.

https://github.com/daattali/shinyjs

I made a package that I want to share with Shiny app devs.  The package exposes some common useful (at least in my opinion, stuff that I use often) JS functions in R, and abstracts away the JS to make it easier to do some simple things that basic Shiny doesn't readily support. I hope others will find it useful

and shiny hasn't actually rendered the element. If you make the element invisible using `visibility: hidden`, it works fine, so it's really something about the fact that it's `display: none`. But I don't want to use visibility:hidden because then the space of it is still taken up on the page. Can someone confirm if this is by design (and if so, then why?) or a bug? I'd like to know if there's a workaround for this meanwhile. I have a lot of use cases where I like to start with something initially hidden and I don't always like to use conditionalPanel for this. Thanks

messages.body_plain:
(Hi Dean, when I found out about shinyjs yesterday I meant to reach out to you about exactly this issue, which I knew you would run into.) It's a feature. The goal is to not spend cycles rendering something that won't be seen anyway. This is really helpful in apps that have a bunch of tabs, some of which contain expensive plots or whatever. However, the feature is better than it looks--it's intended that when the element goes from display:none to display:block or whatever, then Shiny would realize it and start executing the render block that belongs to it. Unfortunately for performance reasons we don't want to just poll on these elements, so instead we need a little help from whomever is showing/hiding the element. If you raise a jQuery "shown"/"hidden" event then Shiny will know to go look for newly displayed or hidden outputs. You can see how conditionalPanel does it here . You can turn off this behavior on a per-output basis using outputOptions(output, id, suspendWhenHidden=FALSE). messages.subject: Re: Disabled input tags
messages.subject_clean: Disabled input tags
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jie,

Joe's solution is really nice and elegant and will work on any input tag that is generated using plain HTML. If you use a normal select tag without selectize (`selectInput(selectize = FALSE)`), his solution will probably work.  The reason disabling selectize inputs and some other inputs doesn't just work is because they use a special javascript library to construct the tag instead of plain HTML.

Disclaimer: self-promotion: you can use my new package shinyjs (https://github.com/daattali/shinyjs) to do this, it is meant to help shiny app developers do these kinds of small tasks with normal R code instead of fiddling with javsacript

messages.subject: Re: Can Shiny work with Micromap package?
messages.subject_clean: Can Shiny work with Micromap package?
messages.body_plain:
Wei,
Looking at your code, I think your panel.att=list is short one panel.  You should have four panels as you specify in panel.types labels, dot, dot, and map.  However, your panel.att list only has three panels specified, with panel 1 corresponding to list 1 for your label panel, panel 2 corresponding to list 2 for your dot panel for landlines, and panel 3 corresponding to list 3 for your dot panel of p_utdtp4.  You need to specify a 4th list that will contain the options you want to specify for your map panel.  Try adding that 4th list and then see if the micromap can be displayed in the Shiny application.  Besides the introduction guide included with the micromap R package, there is an article in the Journal of Statistical Software (http://www.jstatsoft.org/v63) on the package.
Regards,
Mike

Two common causes for this error are:

1) Windows filenames are case-insensitive while Linux is case-sensitive; is it possible you didn't exactly match the case of your data file's path in your source code?
2) Absolute paths that work on your machine are not likely to work on Shinyapps, instead locate the file relative to your app's root dir and use a relative path.

messages.body_plain:
loessPlot should be a regular function, not a reactive. This is because the "plot" and "points" calls are side-effecty. You could put everything up to the plot call in a reactive, but the plot and points themselves can't be in a reactive expression.

doLoess<-reactive({

  c<-physicalCol()
  d<-geneticalCol()
  l<-listePointsRouges()
  if (length(l)>0){
    c<-c[-l]
    d<-d[-l]
  }
  Loess<-loess(d ~ c,  span = input$Span, degree =input$Degree)
  expli <- seq(from = min(c), to = max(c), length.out = 100)

  list(c=c, d=d, expli=expli)
})

loessPlot <- function() {
  expli <- doLoess()$expli
  c <- doLoess()$c
  d <- doLoess()$d

  plot(expli / 1000000,predict(Loess,newdata=expli), xlab="Physical positions (Mb)", ylab="Genetic distances (cM)", axes=TRUE, col="black", lty=4, lwd=2,type='l')

  points(c/1000000,d,col = "blue")
}

# It works
output$loess<-renderPlot({
  loessPlot()
})

# It doesn't work
output$loess4<-renderPlot({
  loessPlot()
   abline(v=as.integer(input$tex)/1000000,col="red")
})

messages.body_plain:
You can use [[-style indexing to dynamically access an input name, e.g.:

val <- input[[paste0('column', i)]]

If you want one observe() per input, you can do that by putting observe() inside the body of an lapply.

# in server.R server function
maxIdSeen <- 0
observe({
  if (!is.null(input$numCols) && input$numCols > maxIdSeen) {
    on.exit(maxIdSeen <<- input$numCols)
    lapply(maxIdSeen+1:input$numCols, function(i) {
      observe({
        val <- input[[paste0("column", i)]]
        # do something with val
      })
    })
  }
})

messages.body_plain:
The context is a set of data frames each having n rows x m columns.
Data can be simulated as:
global.R
data1 <- t(combn(20, 4))    #numCols is 4
data2 <- t(comb(25, 6))      #numCols is 6
data3 <- t(combn(15, 5))    #numCols is 5
data4 <- t(combn(30, 5))    #numCols is 5

Use selects the data frame name via:
 ui.R
      selectInput(
        inputId = "dataName",
        label   = "Select your data",
        choices = c("data1", "data2", "data3", "data4")
      )

The number of columns is variable and is is determined at server.R from the name of the data selected by the user at ui.R from the above sliderInput.
As soon as the data name is determined and implicitly the number of columns via function numCols(), a number of sliderInput is created, one for each column.
server.R

    output$sliders <- renderUI({
      numSliders <- numCols(input$dataName)
      lapply(1:numSliders, function(i) {
        sliderInput(
                    inputId = paste0('column', i),
                    label = paste0('Select the range for column ', i),
                    min = min(selectRange(input$dataName)),
                    max = max(selectRange(input$dataName)),
                    value = c(min(selectRange(input$dataName)), max(selectRange(input$dataName))),
                    step =1)
        })
    })

All sliders are presented at ui.R side by:
ui.R
uiOutput(outputId = "sliders")

At this point, user can select the range of numbers for each columns of data by changing the range from the corresponding sliderInput.
The output should change according to the ranges set by the user in via one or more sliderInput widgets.
Therefore, the application is a filtering type of app.

Thank you,
I.

messages.subject: Re: Display R console log in shiny
messages.subject_clean: Display R console log in shiny
messages.body_plain:
On Wednesday, 29 April 2015 11:49:33 UTC+3, Sam H wrote:
> How can I display R console log in shiny? I mean I want to see in shiny app what is going on, are there any errors, warning, what is print to R console log... Is there an elegant way to just simply display R console log?

This is what I do, in the server.R, let's say I have a function called myfunction() which displays something on the console. If for any reason there is an error we could capture it and pass it to the webpage.

textoutput <-  capture.output(tryCatch(myfunction(...) , error = function(e) e)

if (any(error <- grepl("Error", textoutput))) {
    textoutput <- paste0("Error:", unlist(strsplit(textoutput[which(error)], split=":"))[2])
}

Then pass textoutput to the webpage via renderPrint() or session$sendCustomMessage().

See demo(error.catching) in R, where there is a function to capture both error and warnigns:

tryCatch.W.E <- function(expr) {
    W <- NULL
    w.handler <- function(w) { # warning handler
        W <<- w
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
    list(value = withCallingHandlers(tryCatch(expr, error = function(e) e),
                                     warning = w.handler),
         warning = W)
}

I hope this helps,
Adrian

messages.subject_clean: Shiny Dashboard on Shiny Server Problems
messages.body_plain:
When you install packages for Shiny Server, you need to install them either as the "shiny" user, or as root (which will install them system-wide). Otherwise, if you just install it when logged in as yourself, you're just installing it for you, not for the shiny user.

Here's how you would do it as root:

sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('shinydashboard', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')\""

and here's how you would do it as shiny (I think):

sudo su shiny - -c "R -e \"install.packages('shinydashboard', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')\""

If you want to install from github, first do the above but with "devtools" instead of "shinydashboard". Then run one of these:

sudo su - -c "R -e \"devtools::install_github('hadley/shinySignals')\""  # as root
sudo su shiny - -c "R -e \"devtools::install_github('hadley/shinySignals')\""  # as shiny

Hope that helps.

messages.subject: Shiny app runs fine on windows, but crashes periodically when running on Ubuntu 14.04
messages.subject_clean: Shiny app runs fine on windows, but crashes periodically when running on Ubuntu 14.04
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I have a shiny app that was written on a windows machine (8.1), where it runs smoothly. I have installed the app on Ubuntu 14.04 in order to use shiny-server. The app loads normally and runs normally for about 30 - 60 seconds before crashing. This happens when I run via shiny-server, or directly from RStudio.

A web browser typically gives an error like this:

The page at 10.190.60.131:3838 <http://10.190.60.131:3838> says:

DataTabIes warning: table id=DataTabIes_Table_O-Ajax

error. For more information about this error, please see

http://datatabIes.net/tn/7

When I run the app directly from RStudio, the crash corresponds to the following error (and traceback):

Error: Results must be all atomic, or all data frames
> traceback()
8: stop(list(message = "Results must be all atomic, or all data frames",
       call = NULL, cppstack = NULL))
7: .Call("httpuv_run", PACKAGE = "httpuv", timeoutMillis)
6: run(timeoutMs)
5: service(timeout)
4: serviceApp()
3: withCallingHandlers(expr, error = function(e) {
       handle <- getOption("shiny.error")
       if (is.function(handle))
           handle()
   })
2: shinyCallingHandlers(while (!.globals$stopped) {
       serviceApp()
       Sys.sleep(0.001)
   })
1: shiny::runApp()

Can anyone help me understand what is happening here? Thanks in advance...
